ic_name: LIN bus 2.2A (Local Interconnect Network, LIN Consortium)

clock_and_reset_waveform.XIN: External clock input; ≤ 24.0 MHz; drives baud rate generator.
clock_and_reset_waveform.XOUT: Output of internal feedback inverter for crystal oscillator; unused when external clock is applied.
clock_and_reset_waveform.BAUDOUT: 16× baud-rate clock generated by the baud rate generator.
clock_and_reset_waveform.RCLK: Receiver clock input; typically tied to BAUDOUT.
clock_and_reset_waveform.MR_reset: Master Reset (active HIGH); ≥ 1 µs pulse width. Schmitt input with 0.5 V hysteresis.

serial_frame_waveform.start_bit: 1 bit-time LOW (drives mark→space transition); detected on SIN HIGH→LOW edge.
serial_frame_waveform.data_bits: 5-8 bits, transmitted LSB first; each bit lasts 1 bit-time (16 BAUDOUT clocks).
serial_frame_waveform.parity_bit: Optional 1 bit; even, odd, mark, or space per LCR.EPS/STICK.
serial_frame_waveform.false_start_rejection: Receiver re-samples SIN 8 BAUDOUT clocks after the start-bit edge; if still LOW, accepts start bit; otherwise rejects.

receiver_mid_bit_sampling.rule: Receiver samples each bit at the 8th of 16 BAUDOUT clocks (mid-bit), maximizing noise immunity.

write_cycle_timing.control_strobes: WR / WR with chip selected (CS0 + CS1 HIGH, CS2 LOW) and Register Select (A0-A2) stable.
write_cycle_timing.tADS_setup: Register-Select setup before WR rising edge.
write_cycle_timing.tADH_hold: Register-Select hold after WR rising edge.

read_cycle_timing.control_strobes: RD / RD with chip selected and Register Select stable.
read_cycle_timing.DDIS_low_during_read: DDIS goes LOW while CPU is reading from UART; can disable / direct an external bus transceiver.

interrupt_timing.tSI_initial: Delay from initial CPU write to first interrupt.
interrupt_timing.tSTI_stop: Delay from stop-bit edge to THRE interrupt.
interrupt_timing.tIR_reset: Delay from RD (IIR) to INTR reset.
interrupt_timing.tHR_reset: Delay from WR (THR) to interrupt reset.

modem_control_timing.tMDO: Delay from WR (MCR) to modem output change.
modem_control_timing.tRIM: Delay from RD (MSR) to interrupt reset.
modem_control_timing.tSIM: Delay from MODEM input change to interrupt set.

fifo_mode_timing_notes: Trigger-level interrupts and DR indication are delayed 3 RCLKs in FIFO mode.
Status indicators (PE/FE/BI) delayed 3 RCLKs after the first byte; immediate for subsequent bytes once RDR goes inactive.
Character timeout interrupt is delayed 8 RCLKs after the last RX char.

nominal_bit_time_structure.SYNC_SEG: 1 Time Quantum (TQ). Used to synchronize the various nodes; an edge is expected to lie within this segment.
nominal_bit_time_structure.PROP_SEG: Programmable 1..8 TQ. Compensates for physical delay times within the network: twice the sum of (signal propagation time on bus line + input comparator delay + output driver delay).
nominal_bit_time_structure.PHASE_SEG1: Programmable 1..8 TQ. Lengthened by RESYNCHRONIZATION when phase error is positive.
nominal_bit_time_structure.PHASE_SEG2: max(PHASE_SEG1, INFORMATION_PROCESSING_TIME). Shortened by RESYNCHRONIZATION when phase error is negative.
nominal_bit_time_structure.SAMPLE_POINT: At the end of PHASE_SEG1 — bus level read and interpreted as bit value.
nominal_bit_time_structure.INFORMATION_PROCESSING_TIME: ≤ 2 TQ; starts at SAMPLE_POINT for calculating the subsequent bit level.
nominal_bit_time_structure.TIME_QUANTUM: TQ = m × MINIMUM_TIME_QUANTUM, where m is the prescaler value (1..32).

synchronization_waveform.HARD_SYNCHRONIZATION: Restarts internal bit time with SYNC_SEG; forced by recessive-to-dominant edge during BUS IDLE (= START OF FRAME).
synchronization_waveform.RESYNCHRONIZATION: Lengthens PHASE_SEG1 (positive PHASE ERROR ≤ RJW) or shortens PHASE_SEG2 (negative PHASE ERROR ≤ RJW).

frame_waveform.DATA_FRAME: SOF (1d) → ARBITRATION (12 bits: 11-bit ID + RTR) → CONTROL (6 bits: r1 r0 DLC[3:0]) → DATA (0..64 bits) → CRC (15-bit + recessive delim) → ACK (recessive slot + recessive delim) → EOF (7 recessive bits) → INTERMISSION (3 recessive bits) → BUS IDLE
frame_waveform.REMOTE_FRAME: Same as DATA FRAME but RTR=recessive and no DATA FIELD.
frame_waveform.ERROR_FRAME: ACTIVE ERROR FLAG (6 dominant bits) [or PASSIVE = 6 recessive bits in error-passive node] → ERROR DELIMITER (8 recessive bits)
frame_waveform.OVERLOAD_FRAME: OVERLOAD FLAG (6 dominant bits) → OVERLOAD DELIMITER (8 recessive bits)

interframe_space_waveform.INTERMISSION: 3 recessive bits; no station may start a transmission during this time.
interframe_space_waveform.BUS_IDLE: Arbitrary length recessive; any unit may access.
interframe_space_waveform.SUSPEND_TRANSMISSION: 8 recessive bits after INTERMISSION; only for error-passive transmitters before initiating next transmission.

active_error_flag_superposition_waveform: When multiple nodes detect the error and each transmit a 6-dominant-bit ACTIVE ERROR FLAG, the result on the bus is a superposition of 6..12 dominant bits depending on detection timing.

phase_error_definition.e_gt_0: Edge lies before the SAMPLE POINT.
phase_error_definition.e_lt_0: Edge lies after the SAMPLE POINT of the previous bit.

frame_waveform_layout: Break field (≥13 dominant nominal bit times) + Break Delimiter (≥1 recessive nominal bit time)
Sync byte field — UART byte field carrying data value 0x55 (start + LSB 1 0 1 0 1 0 1 0 + stop = alternating edges for slave bit-time measurement)
Protected Identifier field — UART byte field {ID0..ID5, P0, P1}
Inter-byte space (≥ 0) — between PID and Data 1, and between consecutive Data bytes
Data 1 .. Data N — N = 1..8, each transmitted as a UART byte field, LSB first
Checksum field — UART byte field carrying classic or enhanced checksum

break_field_timing.note: An UART can only handle complete bits, so the break delimiter may be shorter than one bit time on the physical layer. Recommended to use a delimiter longer than one nominal bit time.

frame_length_relations.rationale: Up to 40 % additional inter-byte space is allowed (split between header and response). Tools and tests check T_Frame_Maximum; nodes themselves do not need to check this — receivers must accept frames up to the next frame slot (next break field), even if they exceed T_Frame_Maximum.

schedule_table_timing.frame_slot_definition: T_Frame_Slot = T_base × n (n integer ≥ 1, normally different per slot).
schedule_table_timing.jitter_definition: Differences between the max and min delay from time-base tick to the header sending start point (falling edge of break field).
schedule_table_timing.schedule_switch_point: Schedule switch request is honoured only at the start of the next frame slot — never mid-frame.

wake_up_waveform.block_of_wake_signals: Up to 3 wake signals separated by 150-250 ms (silence). Recommendation: not more than one such block per wake condition.

go_to_sleep_waveform.trigger: Master transmits master-request frame (PID = 0x3C, classic checksum)
go_to_sleep_waveform.slave_post_command_behaviour: Enter Bus sleep mode. Application may still run.

slave_synchronisation.method: Slave measures successive falling/rising edges of the Sync byte (0x55). The 0x55 pattern (alternating bits between start dominant and stop recessive) provides 9 evenly-spaced edges; slave averages the period to compute T_Bit.
tolerance_classes: F_TOL_RES_SLAVE — slaves without precision time base (typical RC oscillator) — use 11-bit break detect threshold.
Slaves with crystal or ceramic resonator — may use 9.5-bit break detect threshold.

bit_sampling_note: LIN 2.2 softened the bit sampling specification relative to 2.1 (per revision history). Exact sample-point tolerance is defined in section 6 (Physical Layer Specification).

frame_response_timing_for_signals.master_node_signal_received_at: Next time base tick after the maximum frame length (T_Frame_Maximum).
frame_response_timing_for_signals.slave_node_signal_received_at: When the checksum for the received frame is validated.
frame_response_timing_for_signals.master_node_signal_transmitted_at: Before the frame transmission is initiated.
frame_response_timing_for_signals.slave_node_signal_transmitted_at: When the PID for the frame is received.
